chunks: Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan said: These two narrations which ʿAlī ibn Saʿīd narrated, stating that the grave-robber is not to have his hand cut off if that was not his habit, are to be understood as referring to when he dug up the grave but did not take anything; in that case, the cutting off is not obligatory upon him for that.

Rather, the cutting off is only obligatory upon him when he takes something. This is like one who breaks in but does not take anything, for the cutting off is not obligatory upon him; it is only obligatory upon him when he takes the property. That which indicates this is what he narrated:

key_terms.النَّبَّاشَ: the grave-robber; one who digs up graves to steal from them
key_terms.الْقَطْعُ: the hadd punishment of amputation for theft
key_terms.عَادَةً: a habitual practice or repeated custom
key_terms.لَا يُقْطَعُ: is not subject to the punishment of cutting off the hand
key_terms.نَقَبَ: broke in or made an opening to enter for theft

ai.seo_question: When is the grave-robber subject to the hadd punishment of cutting off the hand in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This passage presents a juristic reconciliation of reports concerning the grave-robber. It explains that the hadd of cutting off the hand applies only when the person actually takes property, not merely when he digs up a grave or breaks in without taking anything.
